message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA but still aligned to the generic disease target). For PRS-comparable performance, only PGS001784 reports a PRS-only metric (Nagelkerke R2 covariates-regressed-out = 0.014661), but it comes from a pan-trait/global-biobank framework paper, which the provided domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused models unless it has clearly superior endpoint/metric evidence. PGS000753 is from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) with a direct AAA endpoint and reports an OR per SD of 1.37 (moderate discriminative signal) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), making its evidence package more coherent for a standalone AAA PRS despite lacking explicit PRS-only AUC/R2. Remaining limitation: across the pool, most candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index (not PRS-only) or weakly comparable metrics, and covariates are unknown for some (PGS003429/PGS003972), so the visible evidence is insufficient to make a clearly high-confidence, high-quality single winner."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001777","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to the target EFO (alcoholic liver cirrhosis) with broadly aligned reported traits. PGS001777 is preferred because it is disease-focused (alcohol-related cirrhosis in drinkers) and provides the most PRS-informative discrimination evidence among the set via a large risk gradient (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18, 95% CI 4.05–9.41) alongside an AUROC (0.671) in European evaluation. Key limitation: the AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUC/R²), covariates are listed as unknown, and validation is relatively small (n=1,390), so comparability and robustness remain uncertain. PGS000704 reports a higher full-model C-index (0.711) but it is also not PGS-only and comes from a broad biomarker genetics paper (less clearly disease-focused for cirrhosis), while PGS004913 reports a small R² (0.029) without clarity that it is PRS-only and has no AUC, leaving its performance evidence less directly comparable."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001267","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 9 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (trait_efo = ankylosing spondylitis; phenotyping_reported is ankylosing spondylitis or a closely related time-to-event formulation). Among them, PGS001267 provides the clearest PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports both PGS-only AUROC (0.7265, with CI) and PGS-only R² (0.0988), plus incremental AUROC, with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Its PRS-only R² is also plausibly below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.399), passing the sanity-check framing in the domain knowledge. However, confidence is not high because the leading candidates come from pan-trait / framework-style UK Biobank work (the '813 traits' sparse snpnet paper), which the domain knowledge flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation; additionally, other direct-match candidates (e.g., PGS002089/PGS001876) are from a portability framework and lack directly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R² in the visible metadata, while the Taiwanese EAS models report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates, making cross-candidate ranking uncertain. PGS001267 is selected as best-supported on visible, PRS-comparable metrics, but the overall evidence base remains limited/heterogeneous across study archetypes and metric comparability."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001135","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for the target trait \"arthritis\" are present, including PGS001135 (\"Arthritis (nos)\", trait_efo=arthritis) and two additional arthritis-coded models (PGS004477 and PGS004547; both \"M13 (Other arthritis)\", trait_efo=arthritis). PGS001135 is the most endpoint-faithful to the generic target (phenotyping_reported=\"Arthritis (nos)\") and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.53928; PGS-only R2=0.00291) plus incremental AUROC (0.00314), enabling interpretation without relying on covariate-inflated full-model AUROC. In contrast, PGS004477/PGS004547 report only an OR without PRS-only discrimination metrics and have unknown covariates, limiting comparability and making them harder to evaluate as standalone PRS. The overall recommendation remains sub-optimal because the available direct-match arthritis PRS evidence is weak/modest (low PGS-only AUROC/R2 for PGS001135) and the alternative arthritis-coded models lack comparable performance reporting, leaving residual uncertainty about the best-performing direct-match model."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001344","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match asthma candidates are abundant (66) and several have coherent endpoint alignment (trait_efo=asthma; phenotyping_reported indicates general asthma diagnosis). Among the visible set, PGS001344 is the strongest-supported generic asthma PRS: it targets a clear clinical endpoint (\"Asthma diagnosed by doctor\"), reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64568; PGS-only R2=0.05973) alongside full-model AUROC=0.66621, uses only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and has a reasonably sized validation (n=19,857). Competing direct matches either (i) are framework-style pan-trait UKB scores with weaker endpoint fidelity signals despite large training (e.g., other snpnet asthma variants), (ii) have heavier/non-comparable covariates that likely inflate full-model AUROC (e.g., childhood prediction model with full-model AUROC=0.85; family/environmental risk scores), (iii) are incident-only/time-to-event or age-at-diagnosis endpoints (less directly aligned to generic asthma status), or (iv) lack PRS-only metrics, making cross-model comparison less reliable. Limitation: multiple other direct-match candidates (e.g., PRS-CS/PRS-CS-auto and other recent multi-cohort scores) are plausible but often report only full-model AUROC or effect sizes without PRS-only AUROC/R2, so the evidence does not cleanly establish a single unequivocal best model across all candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002755","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches at the EFO level (atopic eczema) but differ materially in endpoint fidelity and in whether reported performance is PRS-comparable. PGS002755 has the cleanest phenotype alignment for a generic atopic eczema target (phenotyping_reported: incident atopic dermatitis) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants), with a reported PRS effect size (HR high vs low PRS = 1.249, 95% CI 1.123–1.391) in a large European evaluation (n=337,910). Competing models are either endpoint-mismatched to therapy-induced ‘paradoxical eczema’ in psoriasis patients (PGS003459, PGS003486, PGS004903) or focus on a restricted severity subtype and report only full-model metrics likely influenced by covariates (PGS001773 reports full-model AUROC=0.93 and R²=0.49 with demographic/ethnicity covariates, but no PRS-only metrics; this makes the apparent performance hard to interpret as PRS signal). Remaining limitation: none of the candidates provide clearly labeled PRS-only AUROC/R² for the target endpoint, so selection relies on endpoint fidelity plus method/variant-count structure and a moderate HR, yielding a sub-optimal but best-supported choice from the visible evidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005168","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All listed candidates are direct matches to atrial fibrillation (or AF/flutter) by trait_reported/trait_efo, but they vary in endpoint packaging and covariate comparability. PGS005168 is best supported because it is a disease-focused, large multi-cohort AF meta-analysis PRS (Nat Genet 2025; many AF-relevant cohorts listed) with a direct AF endpoint (phenotyping_reported: atrial fibrillation) and strong reported discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) plus a per-SD HR (1.6663) consistent with meaningful PRS signal. Competing high-metric candidates include the MVP method-comparison scores (PGS00506x/PGS00507x) with C-index ~0.82, but these come from a methods-focused framework paper and provide less disease-focused corroboration in the visible metadata; several other candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index without PRS-only metrics and/or use horizon-conditioned or clinical-calculator packaging (e.g., CHARGE-AF/5-year risk), which domain guidance flags as negative evidence for standalone PRS quality. Main limitation: PGS005168’s reported C-index is a full-model metric with CHARGE-AF included as a covariate, so the headline discrimination may be partly covariate-driven and PRS-only AUROC/R2 is not provided here; this prevents high confidence despite strong disease-focused study context and effect-size support."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001263","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches at the concept level (all include atrial flutter in trait_reported/trait_efo), but only PGS001263 is endpoint-specific to atrial flutter in phenotyping_reported/trait_reported, whereas PGS001339/PGS001841/PGS002050 use the broader combined endpoint “atrial fibrillation and flutter” (and PGS001339 is additionally time-to-event), reducing endpoint fidelity for a pure atrial flutter target. PGS001263 also reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.617 and PGS-only R2 0.025), enabling comparison and a heritability sanity check; its PGS-only R2 remains below the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), while its high full-model AUROC (0.782) is plausibly covariate-influenced given the small incremental AUROC (~0.022). Main limitation: PGS001263 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-model framework paper (a known weaker archetype per the provided domain guidance), and the alternative (AF+flutter) models from the portability paper lack PRS-only AUROC/R2, making the overall direct-match choice evidence-limited rather than clearly high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000327","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS000327, PGS002790). PGS000327 has the strongest endpoint fidelity: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported are all explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder,” and the publication context is disease-focused (“Identification of common genetic risk variants for autism spectrum disorder.”). It also provides supportive PRS-relevant evidence via an OR per SD of 1.33 (moderate) and a reported R² metric (0.0245) with basic covariates (genetic PCs, genotyping wave), and its evaluation is European with a larger validation sample (n=7,148). In contrast, PGS002790 has an explicit phenotype mismatch in phenotyping_reported (“Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”) despite the ASD label fields, and its reported partial R² is smaller (0.00546) with no effect sizes shown, making it less coherent as a direct ASD diagnosis PRS. Main limitation: neither model reports clearly PRS-only (no-covariate) AUC/R², and the R² fields appear to be full-model/partial metrics, so confidence is tempered despite clear phenotype alignment favoring PGS000327."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000452","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 20 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (basal cell carcinoma), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and strength of reported PRS signal. PGS000452 has clean endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma) with only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and shows the strongest visible performance package among the comparable MGI-evaluated siblings: full-model AUROC 0.632 (0.616–0.647), the highest reported Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0487), and a strong per-SD OR 1.663 (1.57–1.761) plus a high top-1% vs rest OR 3.61 (2.53–5.15). Competing models include near-ties (e.g., PGS000454 with essentially identical AUROC/R² and similar covariates, and PGS000119 with higher AUROC 0.64 but without the same supporting R²/other-metric package), and newer Nat Commun 2023 models (PGS003416/PGS003417) that lack comparable AUROC/R² in the provided metadata and have a less specific phenotyping_reported label (“Keratinocyte cancers”). No candidate reports PRS-only AUROC/R², so reliance on full-model metrics and ORs limits certainty and keeps confidence at Moderate."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002032","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches via trait_efo including the target (bilirubin metabolism disease). PGS001824 and PGS002032 have the closest endpoint fidelity to the target (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: \"Disorders of bilirubin excretion\"), whereas PGS000924 uses a broader combined endpoint (\"Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism\") and a time-to-event phenotype, which is a potential endpoint mismatch for a generic disease target. Between the two bilirubin-excretion models, the visible evidence shows they share the same publication, training cohort (UKB), covariates, validation context, and identical reported partial correlation (0.0716), so performance evidence does not differentiate them; in this tie, PGS002032 is mildly preferred on structural grounds because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (19,768 vs 22), which is generally supportive when endpoints and metrics are otherwise indistinguishable. Confidence is not high because both leading candidates lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R² in the provided metadata (only partial-r is reported), and the two top candidates are near-clones aside from method/variant count."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002786","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All three candidates are direct lexical/EFO matches within the bipolar spectrum (bipolar disorder; bipolar I; bipolar II) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, and similar genome-wide variant counts (~935k–949k), so there is no clearly superior disease-focused study family signal to separate them. For the target trait defined broadly as “bipolar disorder,” PGS002786 has the closest trait_reported/trait_efo alignment (bipolar disorder rather than subtype-specific bipolar I/II), which is the main reason to prefer it. However, endpoint fidelity is unclear/possibly mismatched across all three because phenotyping_reported fields refer to cognitive/behavioral measures (e.g., pattern comparison; DSM5 depression; sluggish cognitive tempo) rather than an explicit bipolar disorder diagnosis endpoint, and the only reported metric is a small full_model_r2/partial R² (~0.0025) without PRS-only AUC/R²; these limitations make the direct-match recommendation weak and keep confidence low."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001033","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches at the broad level of coagulation disorders, but none is a clean, high-confidence match for the generic target “blood coagulation disease.” PGS001033 is mapped to the target EFO term (“blood coagulation disease”) and provides PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.634) and PGS-only R² (0.0578), whereas PGS001826 and PGS002034 target a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO and report only partial correlation (no AUROC/R²), limiting comparability. However, PGS001033 is a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse snpnet score with only 1 variant and a time-to-event phenotype (“TTE other coagulation defects”), which is a notable endpoint/architecture limitation for a broad disease target and reduces confidence that it is the best general-purpose coagulation-disease PRS. Given these trade-offs and incomplete/heterogeneous endpoint fidelity across candidates, the selection is sub-optimal with low confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004153","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match candidates are present for breast carcinoma (breast cancer / breast carcinoma). Among the visible candidates, PGS004153 is a direct breast cancer model with strong reported discrimination (AUROC 0.6625 with CI) and strong PRS effect-size evidence (OR 1.83; beta 0.602) while using no additional covariates (covariates=0), which avoids the comparability penalties associated with clinical risk calculators or family-history packaging seen in some other breast cancer models (e.g., BCSC risk model). It also comes from a disease-focused benchmarking study comparing PRS methods within the same endpoint, and it is a multi-score aggregation approach (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV), which domain knowledge flags as a positive structural signal. Main limitation: several other endpoint-faithful breast cancer models show similar AUROC/R2 (e.g., PGS004040/PGS004025) and some older disease-focused models report higher full-model AUROC but with different covariate sets (e.g., age/sex) or less directly comparable metrics; without consistent PRS-only AUROC across all candidates, the superiority of PGS004153 over close competitors is not definitive from metadata alone."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001301","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All listed candidates are direct matches to celiac disease via trait_efo and broadly aligned phenotyping_reported, but several are either restricted to a special subgroup (PGS000041/PGS000042 are explicitly “in HLA-DQ2.5 carriers”) or use broader/less specific endpoints (“Malabsorption/coeliac disease” for PGS001301; “coeliac disease or gluten sensitivity” for PGS001894/PGS002107). Among the general-population celiac disease endpoints, PGS000040 and PGS000316 report only full-model AUROC (0.90 and 0.879 respectively) with covariates listed as Unknown, which domain guidance flags as non-comparable to PRS-only performance when PGS-only metrics are absent. PGS001301 is the only candidate here that reports explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.82867 and PGS-only R²=0.14224) alongside covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), making its performance evidence more directly interpretable for PRS selection than candidates with only full-model AUROC or partial-correlation. A remaining limitation is that PGS001301 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper and uses a somewhat broader phenotype label (“Malabsorption/coeliac disease”), which lowers certainty versus a clearly disease-focused celiac-specific model with similarly PRS-only metrics (not present in the provided set)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003428","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). However, most reported discrimination is full-model AUROC/C-index with non-trivial covariates, and only one model (PGS001299) reports PRS-only metrics—yet it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper and shows weak PRS-only performance (PGS-only AUROC 0.552; PGS R2 0.00263), which domain guidance flags as a common selection artifact. Among the disease-focused cervical-phenotype study (Hum Mol Genet 2023), PGS003428 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant count (2,894,555) and reports a moderate per-SD effect size (HR 1.33), making it the best-supported standalone PRS candidate in this set despite only having full-model C-index (0.613) and limited visible PRS-only metrics. Confidence is not high because comparable PRS-only AUC/R2 are largely missing across the pool and several alternatives (e.g., PGS000073/PGS000784) have similar endpoint/covariates but their reported AUROC appears full-model and their PRS-only contribution cannot be separated from covariate effects."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001174","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis at the concept level, but several have endpoint/metadata limitations: two are composite endpoints including cholecystitis (PGS001861, PGS002072), two are from a risk-factor integration paper with unknown covariates and only per-SD OR reported (PGS004476, PGS004546), and one is evaluated only in East Asian ancestry with limited comparable performance reporting (PGS005150). PGS001174 is the most supported single choice from the visible evidence because it targets cholelithiasis specifically (time-to-event phenotype reported) and provides the most complete, PRS-comparable performance package including PGS-only AUROC (0.623) and PGS-only R² (0.028), plus incremental AUROC, with basic covariates; its PGS-only R² is also plausibly below the provided EUR heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0214; liability h2=0.1372), supporting metric sanity. The main limitation is that PGS001174 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (a known weaker archetype for external generalization per the provided domain knowledge) and uses a time-to-event endpoint, while the more recent ICD10 K80 models and the portability-study models lack directly comparable PRS-only AUC/R² in the provided metadata—so the overall direct-match recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than clearly high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002237","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 22 candidates are concept-aligned to chronic kidney disease via trait_efo, but endpoint fidelity varies. PGS002237 is the most clearly disease-focused CKD model in the set: it targets CKD stage ≥3 with an explicit eGFR threshold (eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2) and comes from a CKD-specific publication (“Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries.”, Nat Med) with multi-ancestry evaluation. It also reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65), which is supportive of meaningful PRS signal compared with several alternatives that either lack CKD-specific phenotyping (e.g., PGS000859 is tied to a diabetes subtype phenotype) or are framework/benchmarking outputs with weaker PRS-only evidence (e.g., PGS001272 from the ‘813 traits’ framework has very low PGS-only AUROC 0.536 and PGS R2 0.00203). Main limitation: PGS002237’s reported AUROC (0.78) is a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariates (hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use, etc.), and no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided here, so the standalone PRS discrimination cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; this keeps confidence below High despite strong endpoint alignment and effect-size support."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001783","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). Among these, PGS001783 is preferred because it is phenotype-aligned (phenotyping_reported: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto; 884,139 variants), and is developed across many biobanks (broad training_development_cohorts list), which is supportive versus UKB-only sparse pan-trait snpnet models and UKB portability-framework scores. Its reported PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) is available and provides direct evidence of PRS contribution; it is also higher than the analogous metric shown for PGS001788 (0.0163). Main limitation: the pool contains several endpoint-faithful COPD models with heterogeneous and sometimes non-comparable reporting (some provide only full-model AUROC, some only partial-r, some only OR with unknown covariates), and PGS001783’s AUROC is not reported as PGS-only (only a full-model AUROC=0.74 is shown), so cross-model discrimination comparisons remain uncertain from the visible metadata alone."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004621","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches at the disease level, but several are subtype-restricted to alcoholic cirrhosis (PGS000704, PGS001777, PGS004913) or have phenotype wording that is not cleanly aligned with the reported trait (PGS000776 reports cirrhosis but phenotyping is described as incident cirrhosis in individuals at-risk for NAFLD). Among the broadly aligned ‘Cirrhosis’ models (PGS000726, PGS004621), PGS004621 has the strongest overall visible evidence package: phenotype is directly ‘Cirrhosis’, covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs), method is genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,089,806), and it is evaluated in European ancestry with a reported AUROC of 0.68 plus an OR=1.42. However, confidence is limited because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (the AUROC values shown are full-model/unspecified), making cross-model performance comparisons uncertain; thus the direct-match choice is best-supported but not high-certainty."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002034","confidence":"Low","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034) and both align on the target concept via identical trait_efo and identical phenotyping_reported/trait_reported (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”). They come from the same portability-focused UK Biobank publication, use the same basic covariates, and have the same training cohort, training size, evaluation ancestry mix, and validation sample size. Reported performance evidence is limited to very similar partial correlation estimates (0.0562 vs 0.0563) with overlapping CIs, and no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 or effect sizes are provided, so performance cannot meaningfully differentiate them. Given the near-tie, PGS002034 is only weakly preferred on structural grounds (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with many more variants than the sparse penalized regression model), but the evidence is insufficient to call a clearly best-supported choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002042","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001835, PGS002042), both aligned on trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported = corneal dystrophy, with similar basic covariates and identical publication context (UK Biobank portability framework) and similar training/validation ancestry distributions. Neither provides PRS-only AUC/R2; the only visible comparable metric is partial correlation, where PGS002042 is modestly higher (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384), providing limited support to prefer it. However, because both models come from a portability/framework paper and performance evidence is sparse (no AUROC/R2, no effect sizes), the recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000013","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match candidates are present with aligned trait_efo (coronary artery disease) and generally appropriate CAD/CHD endpoints. PGS000013 is best supported in the provided context because it has a clean, directly aligned phenotype label (\"Coronary artery disease\"), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant coverage (6,630,150), and—critically—reports an explicit PRS-comparable metric (pgs_only_r2=0.04) in addition to a European validation AUROC (0.81) with only basic demographic/PC/array covariates. Many other candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index (often with unknown or heavier clinical covariates such as QRISK3 or multiple clinical risk factors), or provide effect sizes without PRS-only metrics, making cross-model comparison less reliable. Limitation: several other strong, endpoint-faithful CAD scores exist (e.g., PGS000018 with high full-model AUROC, and newer multi-ancestry CAD scores like PGS003725 with strong OR/HR), but they lack PRS-only discrimination metrics in the visible metadata and/or have less clearly comparable covariate contexts, so the preference for PGS000013 is supported but not definitive."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001331","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. PGS001330 is a time-to-event endpoint, which is a mild endpoint-fidelity warning for a generic Crohn’s disease target when non-TTE alternatives exist. Between the two non-TTE siblings from the same pan-trait UKB framework paper (PGS001331 vs PGS001330/PGS001331), PGS001331 has slightly stronger PRS-comparable metrics in European validation (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 vs 0.576; PGS-only R² 0.00677 vs 0.00621; incremental AUROC 0.027 vs 0.024) with essentially identical covariates and validation size, making it the best-supported choice within that family. PGS004254 reports a much higher AUROC (0.72) and an OR (2.18), but the available AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUROC/R² provided), so it is not directly comparable to the PRS-only metrics reported for the snpnet models; this missing PRS-only evidence prevents a high-confidence selection. Overall, a direct-match exists, but the choice remains sub-optimal due to comparability limitations across candidates (full-model-only reporting for PGS004254 and framework-origin concerns for the snpnet scores)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005170","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match dementia candidates are present, including multiple models with trait_efo=dementia and phenotyping_reported explicitly targeting all-cause/incident dementia (e.g., PGS000929, PGS000946, PGS001827, PGS002035, PGS004281–PGS004284, PGS004318, PGS005170). Among these, PGS005170 has the strongest endpoint fidelity for the target (incident all-cause dementia) and a structurally strong approach (integrative PRS combining 24 component PRSs; very large variant count), with reported discrimination (AUROC=0.761) and an effect size (HR=1.25, 95% CI 1.11–1.42). Competing exact-label dementia models from pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., snpnet UKB PGS000929/PGS000946; portability PGS001827/PGS002035) have PRS-only metrics but come from framework-style studies that domain guidance cautions often underperform disease-focused models; additionally, their very high full-model AUROCs are likely covariate-driven and not directly comparable. Confidence is not High because several dementia-labeled candidates exist with partially comparable metrics, and PGS005170’s reported AUROC is not explicitly labeled as PRS-only vs full-model, limiting strict comparability across candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002036","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match candidates exist for depressive disorder / major depressive disorder. Several are endpoint-faithful (e.g., PGS000138/139/145, PGS003333, PGS003576–PGS003585, PGS004759/004760, PGS004885), but most lack PRS-only metrics and report only full-model metrics or limited effect-size summaries, making cross-model comparison uncertain.
